epic.intent:
## Outcome
Integrate vercel-labs/agent-desktop as an optional computer-use capability of Dark Mechanicus agents. The person explicitly chose "Literally anything, full control", not project-only windows or an application allowlist. Support desktop observation and the upstream-supported semantic and physical actions across ordinary apps, files, windows and system surfaces under the signed-in user's actual OS permissions. Physical input requires explicit time-limited session consent. This is full control of the existing desktop, not a VM or sandbox.

## Product and authority boundaries
Default off. Provide a Full control session owned by one agent chat, clear disclosure of destructive effects and private desktop content, visible current controller/activity, immediate Stop/revoke, expiry and no automatic re-enable after restart. One physical-input controller machine-wide within this integration; serialize desktop actions and fence stale generations, expiry and queued requests. Accessibility actions can also be destructive: consent covers observation and semantic actuation, with physical input separately approved. Include screenshot and clipboard permissions explicitly in the consent, not silent capture. No per-action prompt once the appropriate session consent exists.
Every action in src/core/authz.ts HUMAN_ONLY_CAPABILITIES (including checkpoint approvals, retry grants, Agent access, Kanban review and reserved deletion/transfer decisions), permission elevation and the agent's own permission prompts must remain human-only. Full control must not become a path for an agent to approve itself. Establish a tested achievable boundary in the first ticket; do not claim that checking an app name, a session namespace, DOM isTrusted, or an instruction prevents synthetic input or shell bypass. Failure to establish the promised boundary blocks actuation release and requires a human scope decision, not a narrower fake completion.
A same-user agent with unrestricted shell already has arbitrary OS capabilities: this feature governs its own brokered calls and provides operational consent/revocation, not adversarial containment. Stop cannot undo an action already delivered or stop tools outside this broker. Never infer that accessibility permission is user consent. Never auto-elevate, work around secure-desktop/UAC restrictions, alter OS security settings, vendor CLI config or agent global config.

## Integration direction
Use a verified version-pinned native agent-desktop CLI subprocess with adjacent platform helpers, managed below app userData after an explicit install confirmation; support Find for a compatible existing install. No in-process FFI or unconditional dependency on a global npm command. Candidate baseline: v1.3.0 release observed during planning; verify exact release contract/checksums before implementation, because main/docs can differ. Reuse live-chat/grant/local-transport and process-tree-lifecycle patterns where appropriate, with distinct desktop authority rather than widening pane.control. Expose typed dm desktop commands to all hosted agent CLIs using per-chat instructions/environment, and an authenticated adapter for authorized external sessions if explicitly consented in the running app. Do not expose a raw unrestricted upstream MCP endpoint. Account for the full supported desktop action inventory, including coordinates, keyboard, app/window management, screenshots, clipboard, notifications and batch; unsupported operations return honest upstream errors. Broker-owned installation/session/trace maintenance is not agent authority.

## Platforms and delivery
Target the application's existing Windows/macOS release platforms, x64/arm64 artifacts where published; verify physical behavior on actual Windows and macOS desktops and packaged installations before completion. Linux support of the upstream does not add Linux app packaging to this epic. Full-control capability is bounded by upstream and OS support, not a promise to bypass elevation or secure desktops.
Keep this epic separate from the paused Hybrid chat workspace epic: source present is a reuse precedent, not proof that that epic is accepted or a prerequisite secretly satisfied. Do not resume, edit or waive any of its original criteria. No production changes, installation or physical input are authorized by this planning session alone; execution uses the saved plan and per-run/native-test human consent.

## Verification
Each ticket lists its own Tests and runs targeted checks plus lint/typecheck for code; each sprint acceptance node runs the project's full Definition of Done once, verifies the combined surface and attaches native evidence. No additional tests-first or Fireguard standard is imposed by this plan. Disposable fixtures only for native proof; no real vendor account prompts, unknown onboarding or unrelated windows used as test targets.

## Execution contract and fixed decisions
The first ticket DM-541 is a specialist architecture/proof gate, not a junior discovery task. It is independently accepted inside Sprint 1 before dependent work; it does not introduce a third checkpoint. Its disposable feasibility receipts name the actual observed OS and do not count as final packaged Windows/macOS proof. Before accepting it, the orchestrator independently reviews a concrete native human-only counterexample suite and a frozen handoff containing: exact public command schemas, request/result/error types, command and nested/global-flag policy table, broker/consent/renderer ownership, cancellation sequence and machine-wide locking primitive, safe fixture identifiers and host fresh/resume delivery recipe. That contract is source/version pinned and referenced by all dependent execution packets. An instruction-only or unproven approval boundary fails the gate; no downstream worker is asked to invent a security design. If any design remains unresolved, fail DM-541 with the exact question/counterexample and replan rather than insert stubs.

Defaults chosen for an executable recipe: Full control is Off on launch; base observation/semantic access plus independent screenshot, clipboard and physical scopes; optional scopes start unchecked. Consent default 15 minutes, selectable integer 1–60 minutes, measured by a monotonic clock and never automatically renewed. A new/restarted/rebound generation requires fresh consent. One controller per integration desktop session across cooperating app instances; no claim against people/unrelated tools. Default upstream observation deadline 30 seconds, broker total deadline 45 seconds, client total deadline 50 seconds. New desktop transport bounds: 64 KiB request, 1 MiB structured reply, 32 connections, 8 queued requests per owner, 2-second incomplete-frame timeout. Large image data travels as owned artifact handles, not unbounded JSON. Keep existing pane transport bounds unchanged.

Stop invalidates admission and queued work synchronously. It cancels the actual active child tree and does not report Stopped or release the controller until termination is observed. A 5-second shutdown deadline that expires leaves an explicit failure/Stopping state and denies further actions; it is not successful cleanup. Already-delivered or OS-queued effects may be irreversible/uncertain and must be recorded, never described as rolled back. Emergency-stop registration failure prevents enabling physical control; the first ticket settles the exact cross-platform chord and release behavior. No unconditional zero-late-OS-event promise from cancellation alone.

Privacy defaults: no upstream trace, no raw content in standard logs/activity, private integration-owned artifact root, 24-hour maximum artifact age and 128 MiB storage budget; delete only unreferenced integration-owned artifacts. Expire old refs explicitly, never fabricate data after pruning. Optional diagnostics need explicit disclosure and remain local; explicit evidence attachments follow existing retention rather than being silently pruned. Full control does not authorize auto-elevation, unknown onboarding or synthetic acceptance of permission prompts.

## Ticket handoff rule
Each execution packet includes the accepted DM-541 contract plus predecessor outputs and exact test paths. Every work ticket now has numbered implementation steps, Given / Action / Expected consumer-outcome cases, concrete output artifacts, file ownership, and stop/escalation rules. Where a signature must be frozen by DM-541 it is labeled prerequisite, not left to a junior to choose. A worker may not change that contract, invent API/error names, shrink a test matrix or replace a native outcome with a mock. Raise the specific conflict to the orchestrator for a draft change. The orchestrator retains review/acceptance; agents never approve checkpoints.

## Superseded delivery breakdown
Sprint 1: DM-541–546 deliver the pinned contract, runtime, authorization, authenticated operations and actual consent/Stop surface. DM-541 and DM-542 start independently; runtime joins them; consent follows runtime; command routing and UI follow consent. The first checkpoint demonstrates the real controls and blocks release if the human-only design is unproven. Sprint 2: DM-547–552 deliver host discovery, private activity/artifacts, parallel actual Windows/macOS packaged verification, independent review and the operator docs. Both platform tickets require host delivery and private artifact behavior; review joins the native results and docs follows review. One full Definition of Done per combined sprint, not per worker. Physical native tests always need explicit current test-run consent.

## Catalog, integrity and evidence details
DM-541 must freeze the exact errors and role/public signatures, artifact MEMBER hashes as well as archive hashes, extraction collision/reparse policy, atomic in-use activation, and the per-host current-guidance delivery table before other workers begin. Find copies verified bytes to a managed immutable runtime; a version banner does not prove integrity. Reject duplicate/case-colliding names, drive/UNC/ADS escapes and destination reparse swaps, not only ../. Use 64 MiB archive, 128 MiB expansion and exact pinned member set.
Desktop stdin/request 64 KiB, structured stdout/reply 1 MiB and stderr 64 KiB; reject byte-limit+1 without content logging. Batch has at most 32 leaves/depth 4, complete preflight before its first effect, per-leaf epoch reauthorization, sequential stop-on-first-failure and truthful partial results. Snapshot refs remain bound to upstream session plus DM owner/generation. Unknown requests fail closed; compatible unknown RESPONSE fields may pass through.
Controller domain is the current OS user and interactive desktop/login session across cooperating app instances, including separate userData roots; neither another OS user nor unrelated automation is claimed contained. The lock identity, owner process-birth verification and stale recovery are published by DM-541; expiry alone never authorizes overlap.
Requested AX/screenshot/clipboard results can be sent to the agent's model provider. Consent must disclose this. Local-only applies to unexported artifact storage, not tool-result processing. Content-free activity excludes titles, labels, filenames, paths, arguments and raw errors. Defaults: trace off, 24-hour/128 MiB owned-artifact retention, referenced artifacts preserved, explicit capacity refusal when safe pruning cannot free space.
Native fixtures are owned by DM-546 (shared Electron app/renderer), DM-549 (Windows genuine native controls) and DM-550 (macOS genuine native controls). DM-541 owns their immutable receipt schema/identifiers; OS workers do not edit shared fixture sources. Every live host (all six, fresh/resumed plus custom variants) is verified in DM-547; missing executable/account is blocked, not a generic-consumer pass. Use prequalified isolated profiles and native-run consent; clipboard proof needs a nonpropagating lab environment and format-safe non-destructive restore.
Vitest currently discovers src/**/*.test.ts[x] and scripts/**/*.test.mjs (vitest.config.ts line 9). Proposed TypeScript driver/fixture/contract tests therefore live under src/integration/, not scripts/native/*.test.ts. Do not change test discovery just to make a guessed filename run. scripts/native/main sources already belong to tsconfig.node.json; preserve strict/lint coverage and extend renderer roots only when needed for the new fixture.
A negative-only 'deny everything' implementation cannot pass human-only proof. Pair brokered negative attempts with an ordinary permitted action and explicitly authorized genuine-human approval of a synthetic record. No real task approval, global vendor prompt or permission setting is a fixture. Native manifests mark each case pass/fail/blocked/verified-upstream-unsupported; only explicitly permitted real upstream/OS limits may use the latter. Mandatory missing evidence prevents acceptance.


## Current delivery policy — one sprint
User explicitly requested ONE sprint for all twelve work tickets. Earlier multi-sprint descriptions are superseded: retain true ticket dependencies and the specialist DM-541 prerequisite, but no intermediate checkpoint. The sole acceptance node covers all twelve tickets and runs the full project Definition of Done once. Product/manual human acceptance happens after completion and merge during real use; discovered defects become bugs. Do not require the person to perform UAT or manual smoke tests during implementation. Agents own verification and must disclose limits; this does not grant physical-input permission, authorize simulated human approvals or bypass the final human workflow checkpoint. Any older ticket wording requesting a user-performed positive-control/manual smoke is superseded by this policy: use agent-executable fixture checks where valid and identify their limits, never claim a real human interaction occurred.

successCriteria.text: From a hosted agent chat, a person can explicitly enable Full control and the agent can observe and operate ordinary desktop apps through the supported agent-desktop command families without an application allowlist.

Physical input starts only after explicit time-limited consent, one controller owns the integration at a time, and Stop, expiry, grant revocation, chat replacement and app exit prevent queued or later actions from dispatching.

Agents cannot use this integration to approve their own checkpoints, grant retries, elevate Agent access or answer their own consent and tool approval prompts; native evidence establishes the actual boundary and its limits.

Installation/Find uses an exact compatible version and verified platform artifacts/helpers without global configuration mutation; all hosted CLI kinds receive working invocation instructions, and external access requires consent and authentication.

Unexported desktop artifacts stay in private local storage and standard logs/events contain no raw content; consent discloses that requested AX/screenshot/clipboard tool results may reach the agent’s model provider. Durable attachments/diagnostic exports require explicit actions.

Actual Windows and macOS packaged end-to-end runs demonstrate semantic and consented physical actions, stale-target behavior, competing controllers and stop/restart cleanup, and every sprint passes the project Definition of Done.

Confirm before network or execution; no PATH/global npm/vendor configuration edits, auto-update or OS-protection bypass. Preserve Apache-2.0 licensing/attribution. 2. Implement Find as human-select → copy complete executable/helper set into owned immutable staging → verify pinned MEMBER hashes → probe the verified managed copy → atomic registration.
